BiblicalUsage: Garzen is the axe, the tool that fells trees and builds houses. When the temple was built, the stone was made ready before it was brought, so that neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard in the house in 1 Kings 6:7. A man's hand fetches a stroke with the axe to cut down a tree in Deuteronomy 19:5, and Isaiah asks whether the axe shall boast itself against him that hews with it in Isaiah 10:15.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the axe is a servant, and it must never boast against the hand that wields it. The temple rose in silence because the stones were cut elsewhere, and I hold that God's house is built by quiet preparation, not by noise.
